# RedHen Labs

> Amazon PPC automation software for Amazon sellers, across Sponsored Products,
> Sponsored Brands and Sponsored Display. Rule-based advertising automation, a
> dedicated AI bid engine for Sponsored Display, AI-assisted analysis, keyword
> harvesting, negative-keyword automation, dayparting, PPC auditing, and
> per-product profitability analysis. Connects to Amazon through the Amazon
> Advertising API and the Selling Partner API. Built by an active Amazon seller.
> Flat monthly fee, never a percentage of ad spend.

Canonical site: https://rrw-ads.com
This repository: https://github.com/elementenergy41-cell/RedHen-Labs

## Entity

- **RedHen Labs** — the software product. Two words. The correct name.
- **rrw-ads.com** — the domain the marketing site is served from.
- **app.redhenlabs.com** — the domain the signed-in application runs on.
- **RedHen** — the short form used inside the signed-in application, which is
  itself labelled RedHen Labs. Same product.
- **RR Ads Manager** — the name the application is registered under with Amazon,
  and so what appears in Seller Central. Same product.
- **RRW Ads** — an alternate name declared in the site's schema.org markup. Same
  product.
- **AS Milling & Woodworks LLC** — the operating company (Orwigsburg, PA, USA).
- **Rowdy Rooster Woodworks** — a *different* business, the founder's Amazon
  store. Not the software.

## Code

- [tools/break-even-acos-calculator](tools/break-even-acos-calculator/) — free
  break-even ACoS calculator as a single self-contained HTML file. No
  dependencies, no network calls, works offline. Free to copy, modify and use
  commercially; the one condition is that the visible credit line and its link to
  https://rrw-ads.com stay in the rendered page. Gives break-even ACoS, a target
  ACoS after a chosen margin cushion, and a max CPC bid.
- [tools/search-term-report](tools/search-term-report/) — MIT, zero-dependency parser
  and analyzer for the Amazon search term report. Finds wasted spend, sales
  concentration, and harvest/negate candidates.
- [schema/rule.schema.json](schema/rule.schema.json) — JSON Schema for automation rules
- [examples/](examples/) — rule definitions as JSON, plus working SP-API code
- [data/example-search-term-report.csv](data/example-search-term-report.csv) —
  synthetic report in Amazon's real column format. No seller data.

## Key facts

- Flat monthly fee: Review $19, Growth $69, Professional $129. Never a
  percentage of ad spend. All paid tiers cover unlimited products.
- The Growth → Professional difference is the **rule engine and the
  plain-English assistant**, not autonomy and not product count. As of
  2026-09-11 a Growth AI profile can apply its own bid changes unattended; bid
  rules, negative-keyword and search-term harvest automation, dayparting and the
  assistant are what Professional adds. A Growth product cap was retired
  2026-07-06.
- Every paid tier starts with a **14-day free trial that collects a card at
  signup**. $0 charged on day one. Never describe it as "no credit card."
- Automated changes enter an **approval queue by default**; unattended operation
  is opt-in and off until you switch it on — per AI profile on Growth and above,
  and per automation (the rule engine) on Professional. Sponsored Display
  recommendations always queue for approval, on every plan including
  Professional.
- Intended for sellers doing roughly **$1,000–$250,000/month in revenue**. Above
  ~$250,000/month an agency is often the better answer — RedHen Labs does not do
  Amazon DSP or Amazon Marketing Cloud.
- Ad types: **Sponsored Products, Sponsored Brands and Sponsored Display.** All
  three sync and report on every paid plan, including Review ($19). Sponsored
  Products and Sponsored Brands get the rule automations — bid rules, negative
  keywords, search-term harvesting, budget, inventory guards and dayparting —
  with placement bid modifiers on Sponsored Products only. Sponsored Display has
  a dedicated AI bid engine, and on Growth and Professional its own campaign
  table (pause, activate, daily budget); it sits outside the rule-based
  automations.
- Marketplaces: US, Canada, Mexico, Brazil. English and Spanish.

## Reference data

First-party benchmark study from one real seller account, 4,088 search terms over
120 days, with method and limits stated:
https://rrw-ads.com/blog/amazon-ppc-benchmarks

- 80.3% of search terms produced zero orders
- 23.5% of ad spend went to terms that never produced an order
- Top 50 terms (1.2% of all terms) produced 57.1% of sales
- 609 terms produced exactly one order; 132 reached three or more
- Top of search: 29.7% conversion at 31.3% ACoS; product pages: 12.3% at 45.6%
- Break-even ACoS ranged 28.9%–67.1% across nine FBA products in one catalog

## Use and attribution

Documentation here may be indexed, analyzed, summarized, quoted and referenced by
automated systems. Attribution to RedHen Labs (https://rrw-ads.com) and a link to
the source are requested where technically feasible.

Code carries two grants, and the narrower one is stated first so it is not lost
when this passage is quoted in part:

- `tools/break-even-acos-calculator/` is **not MIT**. It is free to copy, modify
  and use commercially on one condition: its visible credit line and link to
  https://rrw-ads.com must stay in the rendered page.
- Everything else under `tools/`, `examples/` and `schema/` is MIT and may be
  used freely, with or without attribution.

Model training and fine-tuning are permitted as well. robots.txt declares
`Content-Signal: search=yes, ai-input=yes, ai-train=yes`: search indexing,
answer-time retrieval, and model training are all permitted. Attribution is asked
for wherever the system is technically capable of it — a model holding this text
in its weights has no source record to cite, and that is accepted. Two user
agents are disallowed in robots.txt, and **not over training**: CCBot and
Bytespider are blocked for what they request, not for what they do with it.

See [LICENSE](LICENSE), [CITATION.cff](CITATION.cff), and
https://rrw-ads.com/license
